mainTopic: Can a קרבן atone for a sin done after it was set aside? The מצורע's oil, the goats of שבועות, and the בית דין's silent condition
overview: The amud opens by finishing the גמרא's reading of the ברייתא about סמיכה: a קרבן brought without סמיכה atoned for the person, but not fully before Heaven. The גמרא tries to support this from a משנה about the leftover oil of a מצורע, where רבי יוחנן בן נורי uses the same phrase, 'as though it did not atone.' The proof is pushed away, because there the phrase can mean that one oil placement was done and another was missed. Next the גמרא turns to the bigger question: can a קרבן atone for a sin done after it was set aside? It brings רבי שמעון's teaching that the second goat of שבועות atones for טומאה that happened between the two goats. One answer says the goats may have been set aside one after the other, but that reading of the פסוק seems forced. רב פפא answers differently: communal offerings are only finally designated at שחיטה, by the בית דין's silent condition. רב יוסף בריה דרב שמואל then asks whether רבי שמעון even holds this idea, and his source continues on the next amud.

steps.title: It did not atone before Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its suggested reading: the קרבן 'did not atone' only in the sense of before Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: It did not atone before Heaven!
steps.whatsHappening: This line is the end of an explanation that started just before this section. The גמרא is saying that 'it did not atone' means it was not a complete atonement in Heaven's eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא about סמיכה seems to say two opposite things: it atoned, and it did not atone. This reading splits them. The person really is atoned for, but before Heaven the קרבן is not seen as complete.

keyTerms.meaning: it atoned
before Heaven, in God's eyes

phrases.english: It did not atone – before Heaven!
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from just before this section. The first half was: 'it atoned for the person.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation of the סמיכה ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two phrases into two different levels of atonement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Atoned' and 'did not atone' look like a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: It atoned for the person, but not fully before Heaven.

steps.title: The משנה about the leftover oil of the מצורע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה where רבי עקיבא and רבי יוחנן בן נורי argue about placing the leftover oil on the מצורע's head.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't we learn in a משנה: The פסוק says, 'And the rest of the oil in the כהן's hand... to atone for him before ה'.' If he placed it, it atoned. If he did not place it, it did not atone. These are the words of רבי עקיבא. רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: it is only a leftover, extra part of the מצוה. Whether it was placed or not, it atoned, but the פסוק treats him as if it did not atone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to support its reading. רבי יוחנן בן נורי uses the very same phrase, 'as if it did not atone,' about the oil of a מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, placing the oil on the head is required, so without it there is no atonement. For רבי יוחנן בן נורי it is only an extra part of the מצוה, so atonement happens either way. Yet he still says 'as if it did not atone,' just like the ברייתא about סמיכה. The גמרא will now look at what he means.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't we learn in a משנה? (introduces a source as support)
the oil that is left over
leftovers of a מצוה, a part that is not required
it is counted against him, he is treated as

phrases.english: Didn't we learn in a mishna:
"And the rest of the oil that is in the hand, etc.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:18. This is the oil left in the כהן's hand during the purification of a מצורע.

phrases.english: to atone for him before the Lord" –
if he placed it, it atoned;
phrases.notes: He means placing the leftover oil on the מצורע's head.

phrases.english: and if he did not place it, it did not atone.
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
Rabbi Yoḥanan [ben Nuri] says:
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording, so we know which רבי יוחנן this is.

phrases.english: They are leftovers of the מצוה;

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין נִיתַּן בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא נִיתַּן – כִּיפֵּר,
phrases.english: whether it was placed or was not placed – it atoned,
but it is counted against him as though it did not atone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that uses the same phrase, to support the reading in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that 'did not atone' means 'not before Heaven'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נגעים: רבי יוחנן בן נורי on the leftover oil of the מצורע

steps.title: What does 'as though it did not atone' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן בן נורי means by 'as though it did not atone.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'as though it did not atone' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what רבי יוחנן בן נורי's phrase really means. This sets up the next steps, which test possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if the phrase in the משנה means 'not before Heaven.' So the גמרא first has to pin down what the phrase means there.

keyTerms.meaning: what? (asks for the meaning of something)
as though, as if

phrases.english: What is "as though it did not atone"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'as though it did not atone' in רבי יוחנן בן נורי's words

steps.title: It can't mean he must bring another offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests one meaning, that he needs another קרבן, and rejects it because רבי יוחנן בן נורי already said it atoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means he must bring another offering, but you just said: whether it was placed or not, it atoned!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one meaning and knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he had to bring another offering, then nothing was really atoned. But רבי יוחנן בן נורי clearly said 'it atoned' in both cases. So 'as though it did not atone' cannot mean the atonement failed.

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
another offering
but you said! (points to a contradiction)

phrases.english: If we say that he needs to bring another offering,
phrases.notes: In this case the 'offering' is the oil.

phrases.aramaic: הָאָמְרַתְּ: בֵּין נִיתַּן בֵּין לֹא נִיתַּן כִּיפֵּר!
phrases.english: didn't you say: whether it was placed or not placed, it atoned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects one answer to the question in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that 'as though it did not atone' means another קרבן is needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It contradicts רבי יוחנן בן נורי's own words that it atoned either way.

steps.title: It atoned for the person, not before Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that in the משנה, 'atoned' means for the person and 'did not atone' means before Heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it atoned for the person, but it did not atone before Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the meaning that works: the person is atoned for, but before Heaven it is not complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same split the גמרא suggested in step 1 for סמיכה. Now it seems to be found in the משנה too, which makes the reading stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: the person, the man

phrases.english: Rather, it atoned – for the person,
it did not atone – before Heaven;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first meaning, gives the meaning that fits.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'As though it did not atone' means it atoned for the person but not before Heaven.

steps.title: So too with סמיכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies the משנה's meaning to the ברייתא about סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too: it atoned, and so on!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof. The phrase in the סמיכה ברייתא should mean the same as in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the same phrase in the משנה means 'atoned for the person, not before Heaven,' the ברייתא about סמיכה should be read the same way. This backs up step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: here too
and so on (short for the rest of the phrase)

phrases.english: Here too, it atoned, etc.!
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the סמיכה case. The 'etc.' stands for: for the person, but not before Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the meaning found in step 5 and applies it back to the סמיכה case.
steps.raayaObject: The reading of the סמיכה ברייתא from step 1
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן בן נורי's phrase, as explained in step 5

steps.title: In the oil case, it means two different placements
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the proof. In the משנה, 'atoned' can mean the oil on the thumb and big toe, and 'did not atone' can mean the oil on the head.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, 'it atoned' refers to the placing on the thumb and big toe, and 'it did not atone' refers to the placing on the head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. In the מצורע case, the two phrases can refer to two different parts of the process, not to two levels of atonement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil for a מצורע is placed in more than one spot. The placing on the thumb and big toe was done, so that part atoned. The placing on the head was missed, so that part is lacking. This has nothing to do with 'before Heaven,' so the משנה does not prove the reading of the סמיכה ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: there too (applies a new explanation to the source just brought)
placing the oil on the right thumb and big toe
placing the oil on the head

steps.whatToRemember: The proof from the מצורע fails. There, 'atoned / did not atone' can mean that one placement of oil was done and another was not. So the meaning of 'as though it did not atone' for סמיכה is still not proven from here.
steps.confusionAlert: The דחיה does not say the reading from step 1 is wrong. It only says the משנה about the מצורע cannot prove it.

phrases.english: There too, it atoned – the placement on the thumbs,
phrases.notes: בהונות here means the right thumb and the right big toe of the מצורע.

phrases.english: it did not atone – the placement on the head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof built in steps 2 through 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the מצורע משנה, not the reading of the סמיכה ברייתא itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the משנה, the two phrases can refer to two physical oil placements instead of 'for the person' versus 'before Heaven.'

steps.title: A new proof from רבי שמעון about the offerings of שבועות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new proof by quoting רבי שמעון's question about what the lambs of שבועות are brought for.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי שמעון says: The lambs of שבועות, what are they brought for?
steps.whatsHappening: The previous proof was pushed away, so the גמרא is starting a fresh proof from a ברייתא. This line is setting up the next moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The open question is whether a קרבן can atone for a sin done after the animal was set aside. רבי שמעון asks what sin the שבועות offerings atone for. His answer will help settle that question.

keyTerms.meaning: Another name for שבועות
The two lambs brought on שבועות together with the two loaves

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Rabbi Shimon says:
The lambs of Atzeret, for what are they brought?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 6 was pushed away in step 7, the גמרא tries a new source.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a קרבן atones for sins committed after it was designated
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי שמעון about the offerings of שבועות

steps.title: The lambs of שבועות are peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא interrupts: the lambs of שבועות are שלמים, which do not atone for sin, so the question makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lambs of שבועות are peace offerings!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops the quote to point out a problem with its wording. Asking what sin the lambs atone for does not fit, because they are שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים are not brought to atone for a sin. So the question 'for what are they brought' cannot be about the lambs. The wording of the ברייתא needs fixing.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings, which are not brought to atone for a sin
They are (Aramaic)

phrases.english: The lambs of Atzeret are peace offerings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording 'כבשי עצרת' in רבי שמעון's question
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלמים do not atone for sin, so asking what sin they atone for makes no sense.

steps.title: Fixing the wording: the question is about the goats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא as asking what the goats of שבועות are brought for.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: the goats of שבועות, what are they brought for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the ברייתא so it makes sense. The question is about the goats, which are חטאות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Goats brought as חטאת do atone for sin. So 'what are they brought for' fits them well. Now the ברייתא can go on with its answer.

keyTerms.meaning: The goats brought as חטאת on שבועות
Rather: introduces the corrected reading

phrases.english: Rather, the goats of Atzeret,
for what are they brought?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem in step 9 by changing 'lambs' to 'goats'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא asks about the lambs of שבועות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא really asks about the goats of שבועות.

steps.title: The goats atone for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון answers that the goats atone for entering the מקדש or eating קדשים while טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They come to atone for טומאה of the מקדש and its holy foods.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון answers his own question. The goats atone for the sin of bringing טומאה into the מקדש or onto its קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we know what sin the goats cover. The next lines will ask why a second goat is needed, and that is where the proof comes in.

keyTerms.meaning: Entering the מקדש while טמא
Its holy foods: eating קדשים while טמא

phrases.english: For the impurity of the Temple and its holy foods.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי שמעון's answer to the corrected question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The goats of שבועות atone for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

steps.title: Why is a second goat needed?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון asks: once the first goat's blood has atoned, what is left for the second goat to atone for?
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the blood of the first goat was sprinkled, why is the second one brought?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון raises a question inside his own teaching. If the first goat already atoned, the second goat seems to have nothing left to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both goats atone for the same kind of sin. After the first goat's blood is sprinkled, that sin is already covered. So he must find a new job for the second goat.

keyTerms.meaning: Its blood was sprinkled on the מזבח, which brings the atonement
Is offered

phrases.english: Once the blood of the first was sprinkled,
phrases.notes: Two goats are brought on שבועות. 'First' and 'second' means the first and second of them.

phrases.english: the second, why is it offered?

steps.triggerLanguage: נִזְרַק דָּמוֹ שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹן, שֵׁנִי לָמָּה קָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 11: if both goats cover the same sin, why bring two?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What sin the second goat atones for after the first goat has already atoned

steps.title: The second goat atones for טומאה that happened in between
steps.stepSummary: The second goat atones for טומאה that happened between the first goat's offering and the second's.
steps.simpleTranslation: It atones for טומאה that happened between this one and that one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון answers: the second goat covers any טומאה that happened in the time between the two goats. This is the heart of the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second goat was set aside before that in-between sin happened. Yet it still atones for it. That suggests a קרבן can atone for a sin done after it was designated.

keyTerms.meaning: That happened
Between this one and that one: the time between the two goats

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the line that seems to answer the main question: a קרבן can atone for a sin done after it was set aside.

phrases.english: For impurity that happened
between this one and that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל טוּמְאָה שֶׁאוֹרְעָה בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12, and gives the point the proof from step 8 relies on.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second goat atones for טומאה that happened between the offering of the first goat and the second.

steps.title: By this logic, offerings would be needed all the time, but the תורה spared us
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון notes that, by this logic, ישראל should bring offerings constantly, but the פסוק spared them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say from now on: ישראל should really have been bringing their offerings at every time and every moment, but the פסוק spared them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון finishes his teaching with a general comment. Since sins can happen at any moment, offerings could have been needed all the time, but the תורה did not require it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a goat can cover sins that happen in between, then new sins happen constantly, and more offerings would always be needed. The תורה limited the obligation to set times. This closes רבי שמעון's ברייתא, which the proof is built on.

keyTerms.meaning: Say from now on: introduces what follows from the logic
They should really have had to
The פסוק spared them

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון says the second goat of שבועות atones for טומאה that happened after the first goat. This suggests a קרבן can atone for a sin done after it was set aside. He adds that the תורה spared ישראל from bringing offerings every moment.

phrases.english: Say from now on:
Israel should have been fit
to offer their offerings
at every time and at every moment,
but the verse spared them.
phrases.notes: He means the תורה only requires offerings at set times, so ישראל don't have to keep bringing them for every new sin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the idea of step 13 to its general conclusion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In principle, offerings could be needed constantly to cover new sins, but the תורה spared ישראל from this.

steps.title: The second goat seems to atone for a sin done after it was set aside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from רבי שמעון's teaching that the second goat atones for an עשה violated after the goat was already designated.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look: here is a case of a positive מצוה broken after the animal was set aside, and still the goat atones!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the teaching it just learned as a proof. The second goat atones for טומאה that happened after both goats had already been set aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The larger question on the דף is whether a קרבן can atone for an עשה done after its הפרשה. If both goats were designated in advance, then any טומאה between the offerings came after the second goat's designation. Yet that goat still atones, so it looks like the answer is yes.

keyTerms.meaning: Setting aside or designating an animal as a קרבן
A positive מצוה; here, keeping טמא people out of the מקדש
It atones

phrases.english: But here
it is a positive מצוה broken after the designation,
phrases.notes: The positive מצוה is sending טמא people out of the מקדש, and here it was broken after the goats were already set aside.

phrases.english: and yet it atones!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a legal inference from רבי שמעון's answer in Step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That a קרבן atones for an עשה violated after its הפרשה
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's teaching that the second goat atones for טומאה between the two goats

steps.title: Maybe the goats were set aside one after the other
steps.stepSummary: The proof works only if both goats were designated together. The case may be one where they were designated separately.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they were set aside at the same time, then yes, it would be a proof. But here we are talking about a case where they were set aside one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. It suggests the second goat was only set aside after the טומאה happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second goat was designated later, the טומאה it atones for happened before its הפרשה. Then the case says nothing about sins done after designation.

keyTerms.meaning: At the same time
One after the other
Here, what case are we dealing with?

phrases.english: If they were set aside at the same time,
so it is indeed;
here, what are we dealing with?
A case where they were set aside one after the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 15's proof by narrowing the case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumes both goats were designated together, which may not be true.

steps.title: Is the פסוק really only about goats set aside one after the other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the push-off. It is hard to say the פסוק was written only for such a narrow case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Should we stand up and say about the פסוק that, when it was written, it was written only about goats set aside one after the other?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק commands these goats in general and does not mention the order in which they are designated. Limiting it to a sequential case seems forced.

keyTerms.meaning: Should we stand and say? This is a strong rhetorical challenge.
The פסוק

phrases.english: And should we stand and say about the פסוק
that when it is written,
it is written about ones set aside one after the other?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case narrowing of Step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the goats were designated one after the other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is general. Limiting it to an unusual case does not fit the text.

steps.title: רב פפא: communal offerings are different
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects the proof another way. The בית דין silently stipulates conditions on communal offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: You are bringing a proof from communal offerings?! Communal offerings are different, because the heart of the בית דין makes a condition about them, like רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a new reason why the goats cannot prove anything about regular offerings. He is setting up the source he will quote next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Communal offerings work differently. The בית דין's unspoken intention controls when the animal actually becomes designated. So the case of the goats teaches nothing about a private person's offering, which is designated in advance.

keyTerms.meaning: Communal offerings brought for all of ישראל
The court's heart sets a condition: a silent, unspoken stipulation
It is different

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not saying the goats fail to atone for the טומאה in between. They do atone. He is saying they are not a proof, because communal offerings are only truly designated at a later point.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
You are talking about communal offerings?!
Communal offerings are different,
because the heart of the court makes a condition about them,
phrases.notes: Nobody says the condition out loud. It is simply understood that the בית דין intends it.

phrases.english: like what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 17 weakened the first push-off, this offers a different way to reject Step 15's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the goats, as applied to private offerings
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Communal offerings run on the בית דין's silent stipulation, so they cannot teach the rule for regular offerings.

steps.title: שמואל: the knife designates communal offerings
steps.stepSummary: The source for רב פפא: a communal offering's שחיטה is what fixes it for its purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: communal offerings, the knife draws them to what they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the teaching that רב פפא relied on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A communal animal is only finally designated when it is slaughtered. So the second goat becomes fixed at its שחיטה, and any טומאה before that is not after its designation. That is why the goats are no proof.

keyTerms.meaning: The knife draws them: the shechita designates them
For what they are

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, the proof from the goats of שבועות fails. Communal offerings are only finally designated at שחיטה, by the בית דין's silent condition, so they tell us nothing about a sin done after a private offering was set aside. The next step challenges whether רבי שמעון holds this idea.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general rule: communal offerings get their designation at the moment of שחיטה, unlike private offerings.

phrases.english: As רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
Communal offerings,
the knife draws them to what they are.
phrases.notes: He means the moment of שחיטה is what finally decides which offering each animal is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that רב פפא cited in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Communal offerings are designated for their purpose at the moment of שחיטה.

steps.title: Does רבי שמעון even accept a silent stipulation by the court?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בריה דרב שמואל asks רב פפא how he can explain רבי שמעון with the idea of לב בית דין מתנה עליהן. He begins citing a chain of teachers back to רבי יוחנן about תמידין that the ציבור did not need.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף, son of רב שמואל, said to רב פפא: But does רבי שמעון really hold that the court silently sets conditions on communal offerings? Doesn't רב אידי בר אבין say in the name of רב עמרם, in the name of רבי יצחק, in the name of רבי יוחנן: Daily offerings that the public ended up not needing...
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף is attacking רב פפא's push-off from Step 18. He asks whether רבי שמעון agrees to the idea that the בית דין silently stipulates, and he starts bringing a source to show that he does not. The source is still being set up here and finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's answer only works if רבי שמעון holds לב בית דין מתנה עליהן. רב יוסף plans to show from רבי יוחנן's teaching about leftover תמידין that רבי שמעון does not seem to hold this. If he is right, רב פפא's push-off falls apart for רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: But does he really hold...? This is a challenge that doubts someone's position.
The court's 'heart' (its unspoken intention) sets conditions on communal offerings.
But didn't he say...? This introduces a source that contradicts the claim.
The daily communal offerings, brought every morning and afternoon.
That the public did not end up needing, meaning they were left over and never used.

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not challenging the idea of a silent stipulation in general. He is asking only whether רבי שמעון holds it, because רב פפא used it to explain רבי שמעון.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef, son of Rav Shmuel, said to Rav Pappa:
But does Rabbi Shimon really hold
that the court's heart stipulates conditions on them?!
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the communal offerings. This is the idea רב פפא just used in Step 18.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֵב בֵּית דִּין מַתְנֶה עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's push-off (Steps 18-19) by asking whether רבי שמעון accepts its basic premise.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that רבי שמעון's teaching can be explained through לב בית דין מתנה עליהן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a teaching of רבי יוחנן shows that רבי שמעון does not accept a silent stipulation by the court, רב פפא cannot use that idea to explain רבי שמעון.
